proposals.before: Compared with those who advance virtue and broaden the Way, who reform custom and shelter the people, these may seem small and can be overlooked.
proposals.after: Compared with those who advance virtue and broaden the Way, who reform custom and shelter the people, these may seem small and cannot be dismissed.
proposals.reason: Chinese 不可得而忽也 means cannot be overlooked/dismissed; idiomatic already has cannot be dismissed, but literal wrongly says can be overlooked.

proposals.before: In the winter of the second year of Yanchang he suddenly fell gravely ill; Emperor Xuanwu ordered a litter to send him back to the mountains. He took up residence at Songgao Daode Temple and died within days.
proposals.after: In the winter of the second year of Yanchang he suddenly fell gravely ill; Emperor Xuanwu ordered a litter to send him back to the mountains. He took up residence at Songgao Daochang Temple and died within days.
proposals.reason: 道場 is Daochang (ritual site), not Daode.

proposals.before: At that time the Shouyang Daoist Huixu went each dawn to look upon the corpse and brushed away dust and snow.
proposals.after: At that time the Shouchun Daoist Huixu went each dawn to look upon the corpse and brushed away dust and snow.
proposals.reason: 壽春 is Shouchun, not Shouyang.

proposals.before: The emperor was displeased with it and ordered Yu Shiji and Xu Shansin to expand it into six hundred volumes.
proposals.after: The emperor was displeased with it and ordered Yu Shiji and Xu Shanxin to expand it into six hundred volumes.
proposals.reason: 許善心 is Xu Shanxin, not Xu Shansin.

proposals.before: The Prince of Jin, hearing this, was all the more astonished; he sent a thousand bolts of funeral goods, dispatched a painter to depict his likeness, and ordered Liu Yan to compose a eulogy.
proposals.after: The Prince of Jin, hearing this, was all the more astonished; he sent a thousand bolts of funeral goods, dispatched a painter to depict his likeness, and ordered Liu Bi to compose a eulogy.
proposals.reason: 柳{巧言} is the same 柳䛒 (Liu Bi) as in s0184; Yan is a corruption of the glyph.

proposals.before: When a neighbor built a wall with an inward bend in his heart, Wenxu therefore tore down his old wall to accommodate him.
proposals.after: When a neighbor built a wall that was not straight (encroaching), Wenxu therefore tore down his old wall to accommodate him.
proposals.reason: 心有不直 refers to the wall's alignment/encroachment, not a figurative "bend in his heart"; the idiomatic already renders the sense correctly.

decisions.reason: s0022 contrasts 可得而小 with 不可得而忽也: they may be counted small, but cannot be overlooked. The literal before flips the negation to “can be overlooked”; the proposed “cannot be dismissed” matches the Chinese and the idiomatic.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 可得而小，不可得而忽也

decisions.reason: s0081 has 嵩高道場寺. 道場 is Daochang (ritual precinct), not 道德/Daode; replacing Daode with Daochang corrects the temple name.
The literal field has the same misreading of 道場 as Daode; Songgao Daochang Temple correctly renders 嵩高道場寺.
s0085 names 壽春道人惠需. 壽春 is Shouchun; Shouyang (壽陽) is a different place-name, so the proposed correction is required.
The literal likewise misreads 壽春 as Shouyang; Shouchun is the correct reading of the place-name.
s0174 names 許善心. Standard pinyin is Xu Shanxin (善 shàn, 心 xīn); Xu Shansin misreads 心 and must be corrected.
The literal field repeats Xu Shansin for 許善心; Xu Shanxin is the accurate romanization.

Chapter text has the rare-glyph placeholder 柳{巧言}; CText and parallel editions read 柳䛒, the same Liu Bi named earlier in the chapter. Liu Yan is a misreading of that glyph, so Liu Bi is the correct repair.

decisions.after: When a neighbor built a wall that was not straight, Wenxu therefore tore down his old wall to accommodate him.
decisions.reason: 心有不直 concerns the wall’s alignment (not straight / encroaching), not a figurative bend in the neighbor’s heart. The proposed parenthetical “(encroaching)” is awkward; a plain “not straight” keeps the literal sense while matching the idiomatic.

claimRetractions.reason: Accepted r0006 shows English Xu Shansin was only a mistransliteration of 許善心; the source supports Xu Shanxin (c0201), not a distinct alternate name Shansin.
Accepted r0008 shows Liu Yan came only from misreading the rare glyph as Yan; editions give 柳䛒 (Liu Bi), so no source-backed alternate name Yan remains.
